Vue Portsmouth (Gunwharf Quays)

Vue Portsmouth is at Gunwharf Quays, making it an option for a film and a meal during a Portsmouth day or evening. It is a separate mainland trip from Hayling Island.

Choose your screening

The venue has 14 screens, and Vue’s current listings include its EPIC format. Compare the film, format, seat and time on the live programme; prices and available screenings change. Book against the Portsmouth venue rather than a general cinema search.

Access and planning

Check Vue’s venue-access and accessible-screening information for the session you want, including wheelchair spaces, subtitled, audio-described and autism-friendly options where scheduled. Leave time to travel to Gunwharf Quays, park or walk from public transport, and find the correct screen.

Make an evening of it

Gunwharf Quays has food and drink options around the cinema. Choose the film time first, then plan a meal around it. The showtimes button goes to the cinema’s own live listings.

Blue Reef Aquarium Portsmouth

Blue Reef Aquarium is on Southsea’s seafront, offering an indoor marine-life visit during a wider Portsmouth day. It can be useful when a Hayling beach plan needs a change of weather.

Plan the visit

Use the aquarium’s current visitor page for the day’s opening time, last admission and ticket options. Allow time to look around at your group’s pace rather than booking it between two tight appointments. Seasonal activities can add to the visit, but check what is running on your date.

Practical arrangements

Check the official accessibility information for step-free routes and any mobility requirements. Confirm parking and toilet arrangements before travelling, especially if this is your main wet-weather option. Family ticket combinations and online prices should be checked against the ages of your group.

A mainland outing

The aquarium is in Southsea, not on Hayling Island. It can pair with a seafront walk or the D-Day Story nearby, with the travel time included in your plans. The official website button provides current visitor and ticket details.

Portsmouth Historic Dockyard

Portsmouth Historic Dockyard is a substantial day out in its own right. Ships, museums and naval stories give you far more to explore than a quick stop between other attractions.

What to see

The partner ticket lists major attractions including HMS Victory, HMS Warrior, HMS M.33, the Mary Rose Museum and Royal Navy museums. Check the precise ticket coverage and any restoration restrictions for your date. Some included sites are separate from the main waterfront entrance, so plan how you will reach them.

Tickets and revisiting

The advertised ticket offers repeat access for a year. Read the product terms to confirm activation, included sites and any exclusions. This can be useful if you are staying nearby and would prefer to spread the museums over more than one visit rather than rush them all in an afternoon.

Facilities and access

The partner lists cafés, toilets, accessible toilets, shops and parking nearby. Historic ships have uneven surfaces and confined areas, so consult the access information for the individual attractions. Assistance dogs are accepted; ordinary pets are not. Check companion-ticket arrangements when booking.

Make room for the day

The entrance is at Victory Gate in Portsmouth, close to Portsmouth Harbour station. It is a mainland outing from Hayling Island. Plan your return travel and leave time to sit down for food, especially with children or anyone who needs regular breaks.
fields.address: Victory Gate, HM Naval Base, Portsmouth, Hampshire, PO1 3LJ

Funland Amusement Park

Funland is Hayling Island’s seafront amusement park, with rides, arcades and other family activities. It is one of the island’s natural choices for a traditional seaside day.

Choose the parts of the park you want

Rides, arcade play, soft play and other attractions can have different prices and operating arrangements. Check the current Funland programme rather than assuming one ticket includes every activity. The separate arcade guide covers that part of the venue in more detail.

A practical seaside visit

Use the official directions page to plan the journey and parking. Check ride height restrictions, access needs and seasonal opening before setting off. Allow time for food, toilets and a break from the games, particularly with younger children.

Make a day of Hayling

The seafront location makes it easy to build a day around the park and beach. Hotels and holiday parks below are places to stay, with their own booking terms. An amusement-park visit does not require treating every nearby offer as another stop to fit in.

fields.openingHoursSummary: Booking essential. Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday and some bank holidays from Easter to the end of October 2026, weather permitting. Sessions at 10:30, 12:30 and 14:30; call to reserve.
fields.sourceFacts:
Meet the Hayling donkeys

This small sanctuary on Mill Rythe Lane offers a quieter island outing. Visits support the care of its resident donkeys.

Book before travelling

The 2026 season runs from Easter through October, normally on Wednesdays, Saturdays, Sundays and selected bank holidays. Opening depends on the weather. Call 07720 204685 to reserve a 90-minute visit starting at 10:30, 12:30 or 14:30. Give the group size and a contact number.

During your visit

Arrive about ten minutes before your session for parking guidance. Daphne’s Tea Cabin sells refreshments, and there is a shop and toilet. Picnics cannot be accommodated. Dogs must stay on leads. Wash your hands before leaving.

Admission and access

There is no entrance charge; donations help fund donkey care. Check ground conditions and any access needs when booking, particularly after rain.
